definitions.explanation: A bridge hung from cables or ropes, from a swaying footbridge over a mountain gorge to a large modern suspension bridge.

examples.japanese: {吊|つ}り{橋|ばし}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}る→渡る：02441_wataru⟧。
⟦{古|ふる}い→古い：00488_furui⟧{吊|つ}り{橋|ばし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ゆらゆら→ゆらゆら：04817_yurayura⟧⟦{揺|ゆ}れている→揺れる：01161_yureru⟧。
examples.english: The old rope bridge is swaying.

examples.japanese: ⟦{谷|たに}→谷：02223_tani⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦かかる→かかる：00711_kakaru⟧{吊|つ}り{橋|ばし}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{高|たか}さ→高さ：05327_takasa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{百|ひゃく}→百：00780_hyaku⟧⟦メートル→メートル：02975_meetoru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{下|した}→下：00670_shita⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}る→見る：00283_miru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{足|あし}がすくむ→足がすくむ：18703_ashigasukumu⟧。
examples.english: The suspension bridge over the valley is a hundred meters high, and looking down makes my legs freeze.

notes:
{吊|つ}る (to hang) + ⟦{橋|はし}→橋：02163_hashi⟧; hashi becomes -bashi in the compound (rendaku). Also written つり{橋|ばし}.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {吊|つ}り{橋|ばし}⟦{効果|こうか}→効果：02726_kouka⟧: the suspension-bridge effect, the idea that a racing heart from fear can be mistaken for romantic attraction
